Subject: Post-call: schedule dedicated capacity sizing & technical deep dive

Hi Anika — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock a focused session to size dedicated capacity and validate latency/throughput assumptions.

Recap (from today)
- Primary use case: real-time payment risk scoring (live inference from payment gateway)
- Goal: 95th pct latency <= 250ms for inference, sustained peak ~120 QPS with spiky peaks to 220 QPS during business hours
- Concurrent sessions: expected active concurrency ~10–20 (burst policies TBD)
- Preferred region: US (you mentioned US-West / AWS us-west-2)

What we propose
1) Dedicated capacity sizing call (technical deep dive) to align on: traffic profile, acceptable SLOs, model variant, caching strategy, and any redlines (security/compliance).
2) Deliverables: our draft runbook + preliminary GPU pool sizing, and a short checklist for pre-call artifacts from FinPulse.

Proposed 60-minute slots (PT):
- Mon May 3 — 10:00–11:00 PT
- Tue May 4 — 09:00–10:00 PT
- Wed May 5 — 14:00–15:00 PT

Could you confirm which slot works and who from your side will join (infra, SRE, application owner)? If it helps, I attached a short throughput_profile.csv with the questions we need filled and a one-page pre-call-checklist.pdf.

If these times don't work, suggest two alternatives and we will re-run availability.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the sizing locked and a short tech demo afterward.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri yom@redwood.com

Attachments: throughput_profile.csv (stub), pre-call-checklist.pdf (stub)

- Typical sustained QPS: ~120
- Observed hourly spikes: up to 220 QPS for ~5–12 minutes
- Payload: avg ~420 tokens/request, 95th ~1,300 tokens
- Model: currently evaluating a fine-tuned open Llama variant; we may need guidance on quantization vs. latency tradeoffs
- Region: AWS us-west-2 preferred

We'll try to hand over a CSV export of the last 48 hours of traffic shape by EOD Monday (sensitive info redacted) and will share network egress constraints in the invite.
